title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 410
text:
83. Witnesses who request an interpreter might also try to give some of their evidence in English
without using the interpreter. Judges should be cautious about allowing a witness to answer
some questions in English without using the interpreter, particularly where the credibility of
the witness is likely to be at issue.
Interpretation and cultural difference

84. Judges need to ensure that, where there is an interpreter, there is no reduction in a party or
witness’s participation in the hearing, willingness to speak, understanding of questions and
overall ability to put their case.

85. Practice regarding how to book interpreters varies across different courts and tribunals.
Judges should be familiar with the rules in their own jurisdiction. For the right to a Welsh
interpreter, the special booking system and particular considerations, see “The right to speak
Welsh”.
